text.fr: 1. Le gabarit SECRET : une exigence de ligne en 11 parties
text.en: 1. The SECRET template: a product line requirement in 11 parts

text.fr: 1.1 Définition du gabarit SECRET
text.en: 1.1 Definition of the SECRET template

text.fr: Le **gabarit SECRET** structure en langage naturel les exigences d’une **ligne de produits** (fonctionnelles, de sécurité, autres non fonctionnelles) : une phrase en **11 parties**, dont la plupart sont facultatives. VariaMos propose chaque partie pendant la saisie (modèle « Domain Requirements - AC », AC = *auto-complete*).
text.en: The **SECRET template** structures a product line’s requirements (functional, security, other non-functional) in natural language: one sentence in **11 parts**, most of them optional. VariaMos suggests each part as you type (the “Domain Requirements - AC” model, AC = auto-complete).

src.quote: The language adopts the following SECRET template that allows defining requirements (Functional, Security, and Other Non-Functional) for product lines.
AC stands for auto-complete since the language has an autocomplete service for the template

text.fr: 1.2 Les 11 parties
text.en: 1.2 The 11 parts

rows.fr: Conditions under which a behavior occurs
rows.en: Conditions under which a behavior occurs

rows.fr: « If the text editors are to be portable, then… »
rows.en: “If the text editors are to be portable, then…”

rows.fr: « All systems of the text editors product line »
rows.en: “All systems of the text editors product line”

rows.fr: « provide the user with the ability to save »
rows.en: “provide the user with the ability to save”

src.quote: Conditions under which a behavior occurs (optional)
Family of systems, system or part of a system (Family of systems in this case since it is a product line)
Security Criteria (optional – reserved for security requirements)
Relax requirements statements for self-adaptive systems (optional)

text.fr: Les parties 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 et 11 sont marquées « optional » par le tutoriel ; les parties 5 et 9 sont **réservées aux exigences de sécurité**. Les parties 2, 3, 4 et 6 ne sont pas marquées facultatives : c’est le noyau de toute phrase. (Le statut « noyau » est déduit de ces marques.)
text.en: Parts 1, 5, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11 are marked “optional” by the tutorial; parts 5 and 9 are **reserved for security requirements**. Parts 2, 3, 4 and 6 are not marked optional: they are the core of every sentence. (The “core” status is deduced from these marks.)

src.quote: Conditions under which a behavior occurs (optional)
Security Criteria (optional – reserved for security requirements)

text.en: Sentence form: **<all, some, those> systems of the <product line name> <shall, could, should, will> provide <who> with the ability to <verb> <object>**.

title.fr: Écrire une exigence fonctionnelle au gabarit
title.en: Writing a functional requirement with the template

do.fr: Décider l’**étendue** : tous les produits (ALL), certains (SOME), ou ceux qui ont une feature (THOSE … that include).
do.en: Decide the **extent**: every product (ALL), some products (SOME), or those with a given feature (THOSE … that include).

why.fr: C’est la partie 2 : elle décide si l’exigence est commune ou variable.
why.en: This is part 2: it decides whether the requirement is common or variable.

do.fr: Choisir la **priorité** : shall, should, could ou will.
do.en: Choose the **priority**: shall, should, could or will.

why.fr: C’est la partie 3 ; elle ne dit pas qui est concerné (voir 2.2).
why.en: This is part 3; it does not say who is concerned (see 2.2).

do.fr: Écrire l’**activité** et l’**objet** : « provide the user with the ability to <verbe> <objet> ».
do.en: Write the **activity** and the **object**: “provide the user with the ability to <verb> <object>”.

why.fr: Une exigence fonctionnelle décrit une capacité offerte.
why.en: A functional requirement describes an ability that is offered.

do.fr: Ajouter si besoin une **condition** (partie 1), des **détails** (8) ou une **norme** (10).
do.en: Add if needed a **condition** (part 1), **details** (8) or a **standard** (10).

why.fr: Ces parties précisent sans changer l’étendue.
why.en: These parts add precision without changing the extent.

text.fr: Le gabarit retire les mots décoratifs (« essential », « ensuring that… ») et rend l’étendue explicite. FR9 en prose dit « all text editors » ; sa version SECRET dit « those… that have the autosave feature » : les deux ne disent pas la même chose (voir 2.4).
text.en: The template removes decorative words (“essential”, “ensuring that…”) and makes the extent explicit. FR9 in prose says “all text editors”; its SECRET version says “those… that have the autosave feature”: the two do not say the same thing (see 2.4).

text.fr: SECRET = 11 parties ; noyau = étendue, priorité, activité, objet ; parties 5 et 9 réservées à la sécurité ; la phrase type commence par « All / Some / Those systems of the … product line ».
text.en: SECRET = 11 parts; core = extent, priority, activity, object; parts 5 and 9 reserved for security; the standard sentence starts with “All / Some / Those systems of the … product line”.

text.en: 2. Extent and priority: two axes not to confuse

text.fr: 2.1 ALL, SOME, THOSE : l’étendue donne la variabilité
text.en: 2.1 ALL, SOME, THOSE: the extent gives the variability

rows.fr: exigence commune à tous les produits
rows.en: exigence commune à tous les produits

rows.fr: FR1 : « It is a mandatory requirement »

text.fr: **« Those systems … that include X »** : formule qui **délimite le sous-ensemble de produits** visés par l’exigence (ceux qui contiennent la feature X). La partie « that include X » n’est pas une condition d’exécution : c’est de la variabilité.
text.en: **“Those systems … that include X”**: a phrase that **delimits the subset of products** concerned by the requirement (those containing feature X). “That include X” is not a runtime condition: it is variability.

src.quote: Those systems of the text editors product line that include the font feature could provide the user with the ability to apply the bold font
Those systems of the text editor product line that include the List feature must provide the user with the ability to choose between 1 and 3 list types

text.fr: 2.2 shall, should, could, will : la priorité ne décide pas qui est concerné
text.en: 2.2 shall, should, could, will: priority does not decide who is concerned

text.fr: La partie 3 est « the degree of priority ». Elle qualifie l’obligation **pour les produits que la partie 2 désigne** ; elle ne rend pas la feature présente partout. « Some systems … shall … » reste une exigence **variable**. Le chapitre « Éliciter une ligne : trois stratégies » traite la même distinction (ALL / SOME ≠ SHALL / SHOULD / COULD) pour construire un modèle.
text.en: Part 3 is “the degree of priority”. It qualifies the obligation **for the products that part 2 designates**; it does not make the feature present everywhere. “Some systems … shall …” stays a **variable** requirement. The chapter “Eliciting a line’s requirements: three strategies” treats the same distinction (ALL / SOME ≠ SHALL / SHOULD / COULD) for building a model.

src.quote: <all, some, those> systems of the <software product line name> <shall, could, should, will> provide <who?> with the ability to <verb> <object>

text.fr: 2.3 La condition (partie 1) et le sous-ensemble (partie 2)
text.en: 2.3 The condition (part 1) and the subset (part 2)

rows.fr: événement qui déclenche le comportement, dans les produits concernés
rows.en: événement qui déclenche le comportement, dans les produits concernés

rows.fr: sous-ensemble de produits : ceux qui ont la feature Export
rows.en: sous-ensemble de produits : ceux qui ont la feature Export

src.quote: those systems within the diverse text editors product line that include the export feature shall impose providing the user with the ability to specify the destination file as the object.
<all, some, those> systems of the <software product line name> <shall, could, should, will> provide <who?> with the ability to <verb> <object>

text.fr: Conséquences (quiz 1, question 3) : le mot « shall » n’oblige pas tous les produits à inclure Export ; la demande d’export ne **crée** pas la feature ; un produit sans Export n’est pas en faute, car il n’est pas dans le sous-ensemble visé. Les deux seules phrases justifiées sont : l’export est une condition de déclenchement, et « include Export » détermine les produits concernés.
text.en: Consequences (quiz 1, question 3): the word “shall” does not force every product to include Export; the export request does not **create** the feature; a product without Export is not at fault, because it is outside the targeted subset. The only two justified statements are: the export request is a triggering condition, and “include Export” determines the products concerned.

src.quote: those systems within the diverse text editors product line that include the export feature shall impose providing the user with the ability to specify the destination file as the object.
<all, some, those> systems of the <software product line name> <shall, could, should, will> provide <who?> with the ability to <verb> <object>

text.en: 2.4 Worked example: “autosave” in the introduction and in FR9

src.quote: FR9 - Auto-Save: To prevent data loss, all text editors will feature an auto-save functionality that periodically saves the user's work.
Those text editors of the text editors product line that have the autosave feature shall autosave the text eventually

text.fr: Les deux phrases n’imposent pas la même disponibilité. Conclusion de revue : si autosave est voulu partout, **dire explicitement** la communalité (« All systems … ») et **clarifier** la disponibilité avec les parties prenantes. Préférer la phrase « la plus récente » ne prouve aucun accord des parties prenantes.
text.en: The two sentences do not impose the same availability. Review conclusion: if autosave is wanted everywhere, **state the commonality explicitly** (“All systems …”) and **clarify** availability with the stakeholders. Preferring the “most recent” sentence proves no agreement from the stakeholders.

src.quote: FR9 - Auto-Save: To prevent data loss, all text editors will feature an auto-save functionality that periodically saves the user's work.
Those text editors of the text editors product line that have the autosave feature shall autosave the text eventually

text.fr: 3.2 Fonctionnelle ou non ? Le test de la capacité
text.en: 3.2 Functional or not? The ability test

text.fr: Une exigence **fonctionnelle** décrit une **capacité offerte** (« shall provide the user with the ability to open a file »). Une taille maximale, un score d’utilisabilité, une date de livraison ou un rapport de contraste **fixent une limite ou un niveau de qualité** : ce ne sont pas des capacités (quiz 1, question 1).
text.en: A **functional** requirement describes an **ability that is offered** (“shall provide the user with the ability to open a file”). A maximum size, a usability score, a delivery date or a contrast ratio **set a limit or a quality level**: they are not abilities (quiz 1, question 1).

src.quote: All systems of the text editors product line shall provide the user with the ability to save the file.
All systems of the text editors product line shall have a file size of maximum 100MB

text.fr: 3.3 Rendre une exigence de qualité vérifiable
text.en: 3.3 Making a quality requirement verifiable

text.fr: Dans le tutoriel, NFR2 reste vague : « must guarantee user-friendly interfaces ». Les quiz du prof demandent comment la rendre objective. La méthode ci-dessous est celle de l’app, construite à partir des quiz 1 (questions 5 et 11) : le cours ne la définit pas lui-même.
text.en: In the tutorial, NFR2 stays vague: “must guarantee user-friendly interfaces”. The teacher’s quizzes ask how to make it objective. The method below is the app’s own, built from quiz 1 (questions 5 and 11): the course does not define it itself.

src.quote: NFR2 – Usability: Every text editor in the product line must guarantee user-friendly interfaces

do.fr: Définir la **population** d’utilisateurs et des **tâches représentatives**.

why.fr: Sans eux, deux évaluateurs ne mesurent pas la même chose.
why.en: Without them, two assessors do not measure the same thing.

do.fr: Fixer un **seuil de réussite mesurable** et des **conditions de test** (protocole).
do.en: Set a **measurable success threshold** and **test conditions** (a protocol).

why.fr: Le critère devient observable et reproductible.
why.en: The criterion becomes observable and reproducible.

do.fr: Faire **valider** par les parties prenantes que ces mesures traduisent le besoin.
do.en: Have the **stakeholders validate** that these measures capture the need.

why.fr: Un seuil n’est pas imposé par le tutoriel ; il doit être convenu.
why.en: A threshold is not imposed by the tutorial; it must be agreed.

src.quote: A requirement states “The editor shall be user-friendly.” Which additions would directly make its acceptance more objective?
Under test protocol U, at least 90% of first-time users from population P shall save a document within 60 seconds without assistance.

text.fr: 3.3.1 Exemple corrigé
text.en: 3.3.1 Worked example

text.fr: Proposition du quiz : « Under test protocol U, at least 90% of first-time users from population P shall save a document within 60 seconds without assistance. » Elle introduit un seuil et un délai observables. Mais **U et P doivent être définis**, le 90 % n’est **pas imposé** par le tutoriel, et réussir à sauvegarder **ne prouve pas** que toute l’utilisabilité est satisfaite : un seul critère n’en couvre qu’un aspect.
text.en: Quiz proposal: “Under test protocol U, at least 90% of first-time users from population P shall save a document within 60 seconds without assistance.” It introduces an observable threshold and delay. But **U and P must be defined**, the 90% is **not imposed** by the tutorial, and saving successfully **does not prove** that all of usability is satisfied: one criterion covers only one aspect.

src.quote: Under test protocol U, at least 90% of first-time users from population P shall save a document within 60 seconds without assistance.

text.fr: 3.4 La partie 11 : « eventually »
text.en: 3.4 Part 11: “eventually”

text.fr: **Énoncé RELAX** (partie 11, systèmes auto-adaptatifs) : assouplit une exigence. « *eventually* » = l’action a lieu **à un moment futur, sans borne supérieure fixée**.
text.en: **RELAX statement** (part 11, self-adaptive systems): relaxes a requirement. “*eventually*” = the action occurs **at some future time, without a fixed upper bound**.

src.quote: In this requirement, we have the “eventually” relax statement, which is found in the suggested options.
saving occurs at some future time, without a fixed upper bound

items.fr: « eventually » **n’autorise pas** à ne jamais sauvegarder.
items.en: « eventually » **n’autorise pas** à ne jamais sauvegarder.

items.fr: Une observation finie sans sauvegarde ne **réfute pas** « eventually ».

src.quote: Rationalization: represent the rationalization of objects or document the reasons for evolutionary steps.
Evolution: document the input-output relationships of actions leading from one or more existing objects to one or more new or modified objects.
Refinement: becomes more specific in detail and is in fact more demanding than the initial requirement.
Generalization: becomes more general or abstract in detail, then is actually more demanding than the original requirement might have been.
An overlay relation indicates that the connected elements refer to a common feature of the underlying system or its domain.
Dependency: helps manage dependencies between objects (usually at the same stage of development), often imposed by a constraint (resource, skill, compatibility).
Contribution: Sometimes, the benefit of a requirement can only be realized if another requirement is implemented first.
Operationalization: This is the relationship that refines the non-functional requirements into solutions in the target system that satisfy the non-functional requirements.
Generates (or leads to) problems or conflicts, often due to different interpretations, assumptions, interests, viewpoints, experiences and objectives of stakeholders.
Interactivity: Non-functional requirements in themselves do not interact, as they represent static objectives to be achieved.

text.fr: « Feature A peut être implémentée sans B, mais son bénéfice métier n’est réalisé que si B est disponible. » → relation **Contribution** ; on documente **de quoi dépend le bénéfice**. Rejetés : « seule relation pertinente = évolution de version », « A est impossible à implémenter avant B » (c’est une dépendance), « sélectionner A et B est interdit » (rien ne l’interdit).
text.en: “Feature A can be implemented without B, but its business benefit is realised only when B is available.” → **Contribution**; document **what the benefit depends on**. Rejected: “the only relevant relation is version evolution”, “A is impossible to implement before B” (that is a dependency), “selecting A and B is forbidden” (nothing forbids it).

title.fr: Écrire trois exigences au gabarit SECRET
title.en: Write three requirements with the SECRET template

src.quote: those systems within the diverse text editors product line that include the export feature shall impose providing the user with the ability to specify the destination file as the object.
<all, some, those> systems of the <software product line name> <shall, could, should, will> provide <who?> with the ability to <verb> <object>

statement.fr: Réécris au gabarit SECRET (ligne « text editors »), puis dis si chacune est obligatoire ou optionnelle : (a) tous les éditeurs permettent de copier le texte ; (b) certains éditeurs permettent d’exporter le texte ; (c) dans les éditeurs qui ont l’export, l’utilisateur indique le fichier de destination avant d’exporter.
statement.en: Rewrite with the SECRET template (line “text editors”), then say whether each is mandatory or optional: (a) all editors can copy text; (b) some editors can export text; (c) in editors that have export, the user specifies the destination file before exporting.

hints.fr: Commence par l’étendue : All, Some ou Those ?
hints.en: Start with the extent: All, Some or Those?

hints.fr: (c) dépend d’une feature : « those … that include ».
hints.en: (c) depends on a feature: “those … that include”.

solution.fr:
**Corrigé proposé.**
(a) *All systems of the text editors product line shall provide the user with the ability to copy the text.* → **obligatoire** (All).
(b) *Some systems of the text editors product line could provide the user with the ability to export the text.* → **optionnelle** (Some).
(c) *Before initiating the export, those systems of the text editors product line that include the export feature shall provide the user with the ability to specify the destination file.* → pas de nouvelle feature : l’exigence ne vaut que dans les produits qui ont Export (« those … that include »).
solution.en:
**Proposed solution.**
(a) *All systems of the text editors product line shall provide the user with the ability to copy the text.* → **mandatory** (All).
(b) *Some systems of the text editors product line could provide the user with the ability to export the text.* → **optional** (Some).
(c) *Before initiating the export, those systems of the text editors product line that include the export feature shall provide the user with the ability to specify the destination file.* → no new feature: the requirement only applies in products that have Export (“those … that include”).

src.quote: If the family attribute is System then the align shall use the Centered alignment only

statement.fr: Règles : Align est optionnel ; si Align est sélectionné et FontFamily = System, alors Alignment doit être Centered. Parmi les produits suivants, lesquels violent la règle ? (1) sans Align ; (2) Align, System, Left ; (3) Align, System, Centered ; (4) Align, famille non System, Left. Puis : avec deux familles (System et autre) et quatre alignements (Left, Right, Center, Justify), combien de produits avec Align, combien de violations ?
statement.en: Rules: Align is optional; if Align is selected and FontFamily = System, then Alignment must be Centered. Which of these products violate the rule? (1) without Align; (2) Align, System, Left; (3) Align, System, Centered; (4) Align, non-System family, Left. Then: with two families (System and other) and four alignments (Left, Right, Center, Justify), how many products with Align, and how many violations?

hints.fr: Une implication n’est violée que si la condition est vraie et la conséquence fausse.
hints.en: An implication is violated only when the condition is true and the consequence false.

solution.fr: **Corrigé proposé.** Seul **(2)** viole la règle (Align, System, mais pas Centered). (1) : la règle ne s’applique pas ; (3) la satisfait ; (4) : la famille n’est pas System. Avec Align : 2 familles × 4 alignements = **8** produits ; violations : System avec Left, Right ou Justify = **3**, donc 5 respectent la règle. (Comptage fait sur ces deux familles et quatre alignements seulement.)
solution.en: **Proposed solution.** Only **(2)** violates the rule (Align, System, but not Centered). (1): the rule does not apply; (3) satisfies it; (4): the family is not System. With Align: 2 families × 4 alignments = **8** products; violations: System with Left, Right or Justify = **3**, so 5 comply. (Count made over these two families and four alignments only.)

src.quote: Contribution: Sometimes, the benefit of a requirement can only be realized if another requirement is implemented first.
Operationalization: This is the relationship that refines the non-functional requirements into solutions in the target system that satisfy the non-functional requirements.
Generates (or leads to) problems or conflicts, often due to different interpretations, assumptions, interests, viewpoints, experiences and objectives of stakeholders.
Refinement: becomes more specific in detail and is in fact more demanding than the initial requirement.

statement.fr: Quelle relation (Refinement, Contribution, Operationalization, Conflicts, Dependency) pour chaque situation ? (a) « Chiffrer le texte » réalise l’exigence de confidentialité. (b) Deux exigences prescrivent des comportements incompatibles dans la même condition. (c) Une exigence précise en détail une exigence de plus haut niveau. (d) A est implémentable sans B, mais sa valeur n’existe qu’avec B.
statement.en: Which relationship (Refinement, Contribution, Operationalization, Conflicts, Dependency) for each situation? (a) “Encrypt the text” realises the confidentiality requirement. (b) Two requirements prescribe incompatible behaviours under the same condition. (c) A requirement specifies in more detail a higher-level one. (d) A can be implemented without B, but its value exists only with B.

hints.fr: Pour (d), pose-toi la question de la valeur, pas de la faisabilité.
hints.en: For (d), ask the question of value, not of feasibility.

solution.fr: **Corrigé proposé.** (a) **Operationalization** (une exigence non fonctionnelle devient une solution du système). (b) **Conflicts** : à traiter avec les parties prenantes. (c) **Refinement**. (d) **Contribution**.
solution.en: **Proposed solution.** (a) **Operationalization** (a non-functional requirement becomes a system solution). (b) **Conflicts**: to be resolved with stakeholders. (c) **Refinement**. (d) **Contribution**.

writing.sentence: Some systems of the product line shall provide the ability to zoom, so zoom is mandatory in every product.
writing.error: so zoom is mandatory in every product

explanation.fr: « Some systems » rend l’exigence optionnelle ; « shall » ne la rend pas commune.
explanation.en: “Some systems” makes the requirement optional; “shall” does not make it common.

prompt.fr: En 2-3 phrases anglaises, explique pourquoi « The editor shall be user-friendly » est une exigence faible et comment l’améliorer.
prompt.en: In 2-3 English sentences, explain why “The editor shall be user-friendly” is a weak requirement and how to improve it.

writing.modelAnswer: The requirement is vague, so two reviewers cannot decide whether it is satisfied. It should define a user population and representative tasks, a measurable success threshold and the test conditions. The stakeholders should then validate that these measures capture the usability need.

checklist.en: I said why it is vague.

checklist.fr: J’ai cité population, tâches et seuil mesurable.
checklist.en: I mentioned population, tasks and a measurable threshold.
